input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: The missing or invalid CA bundle path check in cert_verify emits warnings.warn instead of raising OSError, so the failure no longer stops the request.
- failure path: A user passes verify="/etc/ssl/missing.pem" (or certifi returns an empty path); only a warning is emitted and execution continues to configure the connection with a nonexistent bundle, producing a later, misleading SSL or TypeError at connect time instead of the clear OSError.

Reviewer finding
- description: A missing CA bundle now emits a warning instead of raising OSError, allowing certificate configuration to continue with an invalid path.
- rationale: When verify specifies a nonexistent CA bundle, this branch previously stopped immediately with OSError. Replacing raise with warnings.warn lets cert_verify return and defers failure to connection setup, changing the exception callers receive and potentially subjecting a configuration error to connection retries.
critique: The finding says the missing CA bundle check now calls warnings.warn instead of raising OSError. As a result, cert_verify continues and the failure is deferred to connection setup. This is the same operation and mechanism as the labeled defect.
